paper.title: Deletion of neuroligins from astrocytes does not detectably alter synapse numbers or astrocyte cytoarchitecture by maturity

nodes.text: Do astrocytic neuroligins (Nlgn1-3) play a fundamental role in synapse formation in vivo?
nodes.description: The paper investigates whether neuroligins expressed by astrocytes, as opposed to neurons, are essential for excitatory and inhibitory synaptogenesis in hippocampus and visual cortex.
nodes.anchor: we examined the fundamental functions of astrocytic neuroligins in synaptogenesis

nodes.text: Do astrocytic neuroligins shape astrocyte cytoarchitecture?
nodes.description: Stogsdill et al. 2017 reported that astrocytic neuroligins regulate astrocyte branching; this paper tests that claim.
nodes.anchor: whether astrocytic neuroligins act in the morphogenesis of astrocytes

nodes.text: How can the discrepancy with Stogsdill et al. 2017 be resolved?
nodes.description: Stogsdill et al. 2017 found astrocytic Nlgn2 essential for excitatory synapse formation and astrocyte morphology, contradicting prior work showing Nlgn2 functions only at inhibitory synapses.
nodes.anchor: how can we explain the discrepancies between our results and those of Stogsdill et al., 2017

nodes.text: Astrocytes abundantly express Nlgn1, Nlgn2, and Nlgn3 mRNA across brain regions and developmental stages.
nodes.description: Multiple independent RNAseq datasets show neuroligin expression in astrocytes comparable to neurons, with Nlgn3 most enriched.
nodes.anchor: all datasets revealed similarly high neuroligin expression levels in neurons and astrocytes

nodes.text: Conditional deletion of Nlgn1-3 in astrocytes using Aldh1l1-CreERT2 and tamoxifen at P1 achieves efficient and astrocyte-specific recombination.
nodes.description: Cre reporter shows >80% astrocyte recombination in hippocampus and ~90% in cortex; RiboTag qPCR confirms >85% mRNA reduction for Nlgn2/3.
nodes.anchor: the P1 tamoxifen injection protocol efficiently activates Cre recombinase in Aldh1l1-CreERT2 BAC transgenic mice

nodes.text: Deletion of astrocytic Nlgn1-3 does not significantly alter overall synaptic protein levels in hippocampus or cortex.
nodes.description: Quantitative immunoblotting of 12 synaptic proteins shows no significant changes; only Nlgn3 protein shows ~25% decrease in cortex after P1 induction.
nodes.anchor: No significant changes in any protein analyzed were detected in the hippocampus or cortex

nodes.text: Deletion of astrocytic Nlgn1-3 does not alter excitatory or inhibitory synapse numbers in the hippocampus of young adult mice.
nodes.description: Immunohistochemistry for vGluT1, Homer1, vGluT2, GAD67, Gephyrin shows no change in staining intensity or puncta density/size.
nodes.anchor: astrocyte Nlgn1-3 cKO on vGluT1 or Homer1 staining intensity revealed no effect

nodes.text: Deletion of astrocytic Nlgn1-3 does not alter basal excitatory or inhibitory synaptic transmission in hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons.
nodes.description: mEPSC and mIPSC amplitude, frequency, and kinetics are unchanged; membrane properties unaltered.
nodes.anchor: The amplitude, frequency, and kinetics of mEPSCs and mIPSCs were not changed by deletion of astrocytic Nlgn1-3

nodes.text: Deletion of astrocytic Nlgn1-3 does not alter excitatory or inhibitory synapse numbers in layer 4 of the primary visual cortex.
nodes.description: IHC in V1 L4 shows no change in vGluT1, vGluT2, GAD67, Gephyrin intensity or puncta density; Homer1 intensity decreased ~15%.
nodes.anchor: loss of astrocytic neuroligins had no effect on the staining intensity of vGluT1 or vGluT2 but produced a small decrease (~15%) in the staining intensity of Homer1

nodes.text: Deletion of astrocytic Nlgn1-3 does not detectably alter astrocyte cytoarchitecture in hippocampus or visual cortex.
nodes.description: Glial protein immunoblot, GFAP IHC, and 3D astrocyte volume reconstruction show no differences.
nodes.anchor: deletion of astrocytic Nlgn1-3 did not alter astrocyte size or shape when analyzed at P35

nodes.text: Deletion of all neuroligins (Nlgn1-4) in mouse glia does not impair their ability to promote synapse formation in co-cultured human neurons.
nodes.description: qPCR confirms near-complete neuroligin deletion in glia; mEPSC frequency and amplitude in human neurons unchanged.
nodes.anchor: the glial deletions of all neuroligins had no detectable effect on these parameters, suggesting that synaptic connectivity was unchanged

nodes.text: Astrocytic neuroligins are not fundamentally required for synaptogenesis or astrocyte morphogenesis in mice.
nodes.description: Synthesizes c3-c8: no effect on synapse numbers, function, or astrocyte structure in two brain regions and in human neuron co-culture.
nodes.anchor: astrocytic Nlgn1-3 are not required for synapse formation and/or maintenance in mice or in co-cultures

nodes.text: The discrepancy with Stogsdill et al. 2017 may arise from sparse vs global deletion, developmental timing, or shRNA off-target effects.
nodes.description: Authors discuss sparse deletion causing competitive disadvantage, adolescent vs young adult analysis, and shRNA limitations.
nodes.anchor: It is thus possible, maybe even likely, that neuroligins perform a non-synaptic function in astrocytes, and that owing to indirect downstream effects induced by the competition with surrounding wild-type astrocytes

nodes.text: Multiple independent RNAseq datasets (Saunders 2018, Tabula Muris 2018, Zhang 2014, Zeisel 2018, Chai 2017, Clarke 2018) show Nlgn1-3 mRNA abundantly expressed in astrocytes and OPCs, with Nlgn3 most astrocyte-enriched.
nodes.description: Single-cell and bulk RNAseq from four labs and two bulk RNAseq studies consistently detect neuroligin transcripts in astrocytes across cortex, hippocampus, striatum, and developmental timepoints.
nodes.anchor: all datasets revealed similarly high neuroligin expression levels in neurons and astrocytes and generally even higher expression levels in OPCs

nodes.text: Cre reporter (Ai14 tdTomato) after P1 tamoxifen shows >80% of hippocampal astrocytes and ~90% of cortical layer IV astrocytes recombined; <5% neuronal recombination except dentate gyrus.
nodes.description: Quantification of tdTomato+ cells co-labeled with S100β (astrocytes) or NeuN (neurons) in CA1 sublayers and V1 L4.
nodes.anchor: In the CA1 region of the hippocampus of these mice, we observed tdTomato-labeling in over 80% of astrocytes

nodes.text: RiboTag qPCR from AAV-infected astrocytes shows ~96% decline in Nlgn3, ~86% decline in Nlgn2, ~65% decline in Nlgn1 mRNA in CA1; similar reductions in cortex.
nodes.description: AAV2/5-GfaABC1D-Lck-mVenus-P2A-Rpl22-HA-4x6T injected at P35-40, tissue harvested 4 weeks later; qRT-PCR on HA-immunoprecipitated ribosome-bound mRNA.
nodes.anchor: In the CA1 region, we observed robust loss of Nlgn3 (~96% decline), Nlgn2 (~86% decline), and Nlgn1 (65% decline) gene expression

nodes.text: Quantitative immunoblot of hippocampal and cortical lysates shows no significant change in 12 synaptic proteins; Nlgn3 protein decreased ~25% in cortex after P1 induction.
nodes.description: Lysates from P35-38 mice (P10-11 or P1 tamoxifen), fluorescent secondary antibodies, normalized to β-actin and control levels.
nodes.anchor: No significant changes in any protein analyzed were detected in the hippocampus or cortex

nodes.text: Hippocampal IHC (vGluT1, Homer1, vGluT2) at low (×20) and high (×60) magnification shows no change in staining intensity across CA1 layers and dentate gyrus after P1 deletion.
nodes.description: Cryosections stained for MAP2, vGluT1/Homer1 or vGluT2/Homer1, DAPI; intensity normalized to MAP2 and control average.
nodes.anchor: vGluT1 and Homer1 staining intensities were not altered by loss of astrocytic Nlgn1-3 at P1

nodes.text: Hippocampal inhibitory synapse IHC (GAD67, Gephyrin) shows no change in staining intensity; high-magnification puncta density and size in CA1 S. radiatum unchanged; matched pre-post puncta unchanged.
nodes.description: Confocal imaging at ×20 and ×60; puncta quantified in CA1 S. radiatum.
nodes.anchor: Both were not changed in astro-Nlgn123 cKO mice compared to control mice

nodes.text: Slice electrophysiology in CA1 pyramidal neurons shows no change in mEPSC/mIPSC amplitude, frequency, rise/decay times, or membrane properties after P1 deletion.
nodes.description: Acute slices at P44-50, whole-cell voltage clamp at -70 mV, TTX, picrotoxin for mEPSCs; TTX, CNQX, D-AP5 for mIPSCs.
nodes.anchor: The amplitude, frequency, and kinetics of mEPSCs and mIPSCs were not changed by deletion of astrocytic Nlgn1-3

nodes.text: Visual cortex L4 IHC shows no change in vGluT1, vGluT2, GAD67, Gephyrin intensity; Homer1 intensity decreased ~15%; inhibitory puncta density unchanged.
nodes.description: Cryosections at P35 after P1 tamoxifen, stained for MAP2, vGluT1/Homer1 or vGluT2/Homer1 or GAD67/Gephyrin, ×60 confocal.
nodes.anchor: loss of astrocytic neuroligins had no effect on the staining intensity of vGluT1 or vGluT2 but produced a small decrease (~15%) in the staining intensity of Homer1

nodes.text: Glial protein immunoblot shows no major changes; GFAP IHC across hippocampal layers shows no alteration in astro-Nlgn123 cKO at P35.
nodes.description: Lysates and sections from P1-induced mice at P35; GFAP intensity normalized to control S. oriens average.
nodes.anchor: we failed to uncover major changes

nodes.text: 3D astrocyte volume reconstruction from AAV-GFAP-Lck-mVenus labeled cells shows no difference in CA1 S. radiatum or V1 L4 astrocyte volumes at P35.
nodes.description: Stereotactic AAV injection at P21, 100 μm vibratome sections, Imaris 3D rendering, blinded analysis.
nodes.anchor: Quantifications of these volumes did not uncover any differences between astro-Nlgn123 cKO and control mice

nodes.text: qPCR on mouse glia infected with Ubc-Cre-EGFP lentivirus shows near-complete deletion of Nlgn1-4 mRNA compared to Ubc-Flp-EGFP control.
nodes.description: Primary glia from P7 Nlgn1234 cKO mice, lentiviral Cre/ΔCre at DIV4, qPCR at DIV8.
nodes.anchor: qRT-PCR measurements confirmed that the deletion of all neuroligins in the glia was nearly complete

nodes.text: Human iN neurons on neuroligin-deficient mouse glia show no change in mEPSC frequency or amplitude compared to control glia.
nodes.description: H1 hESC-derived NGN2-induced neurons plated on glia at DIV8, recorded at ~DIV42; TTX and PTX in bath.
nodes.anchor: Quantifications of the frequency or amplitude of mEPSCs, however, demonstrated that the glial deletions of all neuroligins had no detectable effect on these parameters

nodes.text: RNAseq analysis of neuroligin expression in astrocytes using published datasets.
nodes.description: Re-analysis of six public RNAseq datasets (four single-cell, two bulk) to quantify Nlgn1-3 expression across cell types and brain regions.
nodes.anchor: We quantified Nlgn1, Nlgn2, and Nlgn3 mRNA transcripts in astrocytes and other cell types in the mouse hippocampus and cortex

nodes.text: Generation and validation of astrocyte-specific Nlgn1-3 conditional knockout mice.
nodes.description: Aldh1l1-CreERT2 x Nlgn1-3 cKO breeding, tamoxifen at P1 or P10-11, Cre reporter (Ai14) and viral RiboTag validation of recombination efficiency and specificity.
nodes.anchor: We generated mice that enable the inducible conditional deletion of astrocytic Nlgn1, Nlgn2, and Nlgn3

nodes.text: Immunoblot analysis of synaptic and neuroligin proteins in astro-Nlgn123 cKO vs control.
nodes.description: Hippocampal and cortical lysates from P35-38 mice after P10-11 or P1 tamoxifen; quantitative immunoblotting for 12 synaptic proteins and neuroligins.
nodes.anchor: We collected hippocampal and cortical lysates from the brains of astro-Nlgn123 cKO mice and from their Cre-negative littermates

nodes.text: Hippocampal immunohistochemistry for excitatory and inhibitory synapses.
nodes.description: Cryosections at P35 after P1 tamoxifen, stained for vGluT1/Homer1, vGluT2/Homer1, GAD67/Gephyrin; confocal imaging at ×20 and ×60, intensity and puncta quantification.
nodes.anchor: we labeled cryosections from the brains of littermate astro-Nlgn123 cKO and control mice at P35 after P1 induction of Cre-recombinase with antibodies

nodes.text: Hippocampal slice electrophysiology of basal synaptic transmission.
nodes.description: Acute slices from P44-50 mice after P1 tamoxifen; whole-cell voltage clamp of CA1 pyramidal neurons; mEPSC and mIPSC recording in TTX with appropriate blockers.
nodes.anchor: We produced acute slices from littermate astro-Nlgn123 cKO and control mice at P44-P50 after P1 tamoxifen injections and performed patch-clamp recordings

nodes.text: Visual cortex immunohistochemistry for excitatory and inhibitory synapses.
nodes.description: V1 L4 cryosections at P35 after P1 tamoxifen; stained for vGluT1/Homer1, vGluT2/Homer1, GAD67/Gephyrin; ×60 confocal imaging and quantification.
nodes.anchor: We obtained cryosections of the visual cortex containing area V1 from astro-Nlgn123 cKO and littermate control mice at P35 after the mice had been injected with tamoxifen at P1

nodes.text: Astrocyte protein analysis and GFAP immunohistochemistry.
nodes.description: Immunoblot of glial proteins and GFAP IHC across hippocampal layers in P1-induced mice at P35.
nodes.anchor: we measured the levels of a series of glial proteins in lysates of the hippocampus and cortex

nodes.text: Astrocyte morphology reconstruction via AAV-mediated membrane labeling.
nodes.description: AAV-GFAP-Lck-mVenus injected at P21 into hippocampus or V1 of P1-induced mice; 100 μm sections at P35, Imaris 3D volume reconstruction.
nodes.anchor: we applied tamoxifen to astro-Nlgn123 cKO and control mice at P1 and stereotactically injected AAVs expressing membrane-targeted mVenus under control of the GFAP promoter into their hippocampus or primary visual cortex at P21

nodes.text: Human neuron-mouse glia co-culture with glial neuroligin deletion.
nodes.description: Mouse glia from P7 Nlgn1234 cKO mice infected with Ubc-Cre-EGFP or Ubc-Flp-EGFP lentivirus; human iN neurons plated on glia; mEPSC recording at ~DIV42.
nodes.anchor: We infected glia cultured from newborn mice with lentiviruses expressing inactive (ΔCre) or active Cre-recombinase (Cre), then added human neurons

nodes.text: Re-analysis of public single-cell and bulk RNAseq datasets for cell-type-specific neuroligin expression.
nodes.description: Datasets: Saunders et al. 2018 (DropViz), Tabula Muris 2018, Zhang et al. 2014, Zeisel et al. 2018, Chai et al. 2017 (RiboTag), Clarke et al. 2018 (RiboTag). Quantification of Nlgn1-3 mRNA levels in neurons, astrocytes, OPCs, microglia.
nodes.anchor: We quantified Nlgn1, Nlgn2, and Nlgn3 mRNA transcripts in astrocytes and other cell types in the mouse hippocampus and cortex in the single-cell RNAseq datasets

nodes.text: Aldh1l1-CreERT2 x Nlgn1-3 cKO breeding with tamoxifen induction at P1 (subcutaneous, 20 μl) or P10-11 (intraperitoneal, 2×30 μl).
nodes.description: Mice on mixed CD1/C57BL/6 background; littermate Cre+ (cKO) and Cre- (control); analysis at P35+.
nodes.anchor: Mice were injected with tamoxifen intraperitoneally at postnatal days 10 and 11 (P10 and P11) or subcutaneously at postnatal day 1 (P1)

nodes.text: Cre reporter validation using Ai14 tdTomato mice with immunostaining for NeuN and S100β.
nodes.description: P1 tamoxifen, analysis at P35; quantification of tdTomato+ cells in CA1 sublayers, dentate gyrus, V1 L4.
nodes.anchor: Cre-recombination was visualized in the hippocampus (D) and primary visual cortex (E) via expression of tdT in reporter mice

nodes.text: Viral RiboTag method: AAV2/5-GfaABC1D-Lck-mVenus-P2A-Rpl22-HA-4x6T injection, microdissection, HA immunoprecipitation, qRT-PCR.
nodes.description: Injected at P35-40 into CA1; 4 weeks later acute slices, Lck-mVenus+ confirmation, CA1/cortex microdissection, HA magnetic beads, qRT-PCR with PrimeTime assays for cell markers and Nlgn1-3 floxed exons.
nodes.anchor: AAVs (AAV2/5) encoding the RiboTag (Rpl22-HA) and Lck-mVenus driven by the astrocyte-specific GfaABC1D promoter and additionally including a 4x6T cassette of mIR-124 targeting sequences

nodes.text: Quantitative immunoblotting with fluorescent secondary antibodies and β-actin normalization.
nodes.description: RIPA lysis, BCA assay, Criterion TGX 4-20% gels, nitrocellulose transfer, LI-COR Odyssey CLx imaging, Image Studio Lite quantification.
nodes.anchor: Proteins were quantified on immunoblots using fluorescent secondary antibodies, with protein levels normalized to β-actin and then to control levels

nodes.text: Immunohistochemistry on cryosections with confocal imaging and MAP2-normalized quantification.
nodes.description: Perfusion, 4% PFA, 35 μm cryosections, blocking, primary/secondary antibodies, DAPI, Nikon confocal ×20/×60, NIS-Elements analysis blinded, intensity normalized to MAP2 then to control average.
nodes.anchor: Sections were counterstained with DAPI. Images of the hippocampus and primary visual cortex were taken with a Nikon confocal microscope using either the 20X air objective or 60X oil objective

nodes.text: Slice electrophysiology: acute hippocampal slices, whole-cell voltage clamp, mEPSC/mIPSC recording with pharmacological isolation.
nodes.description: 300 μm slices, sucrose cutting solution, aCSF recovery, MultiClamp 700B, DigiData 1440, Clampex 10.7; mEPSCs: TTX + picrotoxin; mIPSCs: TTX + CNQX + D-AP5; Cs-based internals.
nodes.anchor: Whole-cell voltage clamp recordings were performed on CA1 pyramidal neurons while clamping the cells at -70 mV

nodes.text: Astrocyte morphology reconstruction: AAV-GFAP-Lck-mVenus stereotactic injection, vibratome sectioning, Imaris 3D rendering.
nodes.description: P21 injection (CA1: AP -1.8, ML ±1.15, DV -1.4; V1: AP -3.99, ML ±2.6, DV -1.5), 0.5 μl at 0.15 μl/min; P35 perfusion, 100 μm sections, Zeiss Airy-Scan, blinded Imaris reconstruction.
nodes.anchor: stereotactically injected AAVs expressing membrane-targeted mVenus under control of the GFAP promoter into their hippocampus or primary visual cortex at P21

nodes.text: Human iN neuron generation: H1 hESCs, NGN2/rtTA lentivirus, doxycycline induction, puromycin selection.
nodes.description: H1 cells at 70-80% confluence, Accutase dissociation, lentiviral transduction, induction medium with BDNF/NT-3/laminin/doxycycline, puromycin days 2-4, plating on glia day 5.
nodes.anchor: H1 human embryonic stem cells were maintained under feeder-free conditions in StemFlex medium. For neuronal induction, H1 cells at 70-80% confluence were dissociated into single cells using Accutase

nodes.text: Mouse glia culture and lentiviral Cre/ΔCre infection for neuroligin deletion.
nodes.description: P7 cortical plate glia in DMEM/10% FBS; DIV4 infection with Ubc-Cre-EGFP or Ubc-Flp-EGFP; AraC at DIV4; qPCR verification at DIV8.
nodes.anchor: Primary astrocytes were prepared from the cortical plate of postnatal day 7 Nlgn1234 conditional knockout mice and plated onto glass coverslips. At DIV4, astrocyte cultures were infected with either Ubc-Flp-EGFP lentivirus as control or Ubc-Cre-EGFP lentiv

nodes.text: Co-culture electrophysiology: human neurons on glia, whole-cell voltage clamp, mEPSC recording with TTX and PTX.
nodes.description: Recordings at ~DIV42; extracellular solution with TTX (1 μM) and PTX (50 μM); CsCl-based internal; Clampfit template search analysis.
nodes.anchor: Miniature EPSCs were recorded at a holding potential of -60 mV in extracellular solution containing... TTX (1 μM) to block action potential-dependent synaptic release, together with GABAA receptor antagonist PTX (50 μM)

nodes.text: Golf et al. 2023, eLife, DOI: 10.7554/eLife.87589
nodes.description: The paper reporting the studies decomposed here.
nodes.anchor: Golf et al. eLife 2023;12:RP87589. DOI: https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.87589

nodes.text: Identify the non-synaptic roles of astrocytic neuroligins.
nodes.description: The paper concludes that astrocytic neuroligins likely perform other important roles that remain to be discovered, citing recent studies on Nlgn3 in social behavior.
nodes.anchor: it seems probable that neuroligins perform other important roles in astrocytes that remain to be identified

nodes.text: Develop improved tools for temporally defined manipulation of genes in astrocytes to discover non-synaptic roles.
nodes.description: Authors call for continual advances in astrocyte-access tools and genetic models for temporal manipulation.
nodes.anchor: Continual advances in the tools available to access astrocytes, in concert with genetic models that allow temporally defined manipulation of genes, will be key to discovering these roles
